record.paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in the theory of permanents
record.context_brief: Permanent analogue of Oppenheim-type Schur product inequality
record.original_question: For n x n positive semidefinite matrices A=(a_ij) and B=(b_ij), let A o B denote their Schur product, meaning the entrywise product (a_ij b_ij). Does the permanent inequality per(A o B) <= per(A) b_11 b_22 ... b_nn always hold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A=(a_{ij})$ and $B=(b_{ij})$ be $n\times n$ complex positive semidefinite Hermitian matrices, and let $A\circ B=(a_{ij}b_{ij})$ denote their Schur (Hadamard, entrywise) product. The permanent of an $n\times n$ matrix $M=(m_{ij})$ is defined by
$$\operatorname{per}(M)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\prod_{i=1}^{n}m_{i,\sigma(i)},$$
where $S_n$ is the symmetric group on $\{1,\dots,n\}$. Determine whether the inequality
$$\operatorname{per}(A\circ B)\;\le\;\operatorname{per}(A)\,\prod_{i=1}^{n}b_{ii}$$
holds for every pair of $n\times n$ positive semidefinite Hermitian matrices $A$ and $B$ and every positive integer $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Bapat–Sunder conjecture asking whether per(A∘B) ≤ per(A)∏ b_ii holds for all positive semidefinite Hermitian A, B has been disproved by S. W. Drury, who produced an explicit counterexample with 7×7 positive semidefinite matrices (rank-2) yielding per(A∘B)/(per(A)∏ b_jj) = 1237/1152 > 1. Thus the inequality fails in general.

status_evidence.title: A counterexample to a question of Bapat and Sunder
status_evidence.snippet: Drury constructs a 7x7 positive semidefinite counterexample to the Bapat-Sunder permanent inequality.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured inequality per(A∘B) ≤ per(A) ∏ b_ii fails; a counterexample exists.

status_evidence.title: A logical implication between two conjectures on matrix permanents
status_evidence.snippet: Drury has disproved both Bapat–Sunder conjectures on permanents of positive semidefinite matrices.
status_evidence.claim: The Bapat–Sunder conjecture has been disproved.
